The *Pubbakammapilotikabuddhaapadāna* (Tha Ap 392) is a verse text belonging to the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the work across five languages [SuttaCentral].
DharmaNexus identifies extensive text reuse across the Pali commentarial and subcommentarial tradition. In particular, nearly the entire text (§1.2–33.4) is preserved or quoted verbatim in the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Aṅguttaranikāye Aṭṭhakanipāta-ṭīkā*, while significant portions are shared with the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* (notably §10.2–14.4), the *Sagāthāvagga-ṭīkā*, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-ṭīkā*, and the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects text reuse and shared narrative material between this text and several Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese canonical sources, particularly Vinaya accounts of past karma [DharmaNexus]. These include the Sanskrit *Bhaiṣajyavastu* and *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (Degé D0001-2 and D0001-3), the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna*, the Tibetan *Śrīgupta-nāma-sūtra* and *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra*, as well as Chinese translations such as the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and *Gu laishi shi jing* (T 44) [DharmaNexus].
